packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-07 -- unverified image reading (first reader)

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)

Two faces, each shown in a reduced overview with a colour checker and cm scale:
- image-001.jpg: overview of face A (modern pencil note at right edge of the
  strip reads "Stams, STA, Frag. 94 r" or similar -- a shelf/fragment label, not
  medieval text).
- image-006.jpg: overview of face B (modern pencil note at bottom centre
  "Stams, StA, Frg. 94 v" or similar).
Tiles: image-002..005 presumably cover face A left to right; image-007..010
face B left to right (to be confirmed as each tile is viewed).

Observations: a horizontal strip of paper or parchment c. 32 cm wide x 7 cm
high, landscape orientation as photographed. Text is in a rapid late-medieval
cursive in brown ink, in two written blocks, one left (c. x 550-870 in the
overview) and one right (c. x 1070-1390), separated by a blank central area
that looks like a fold/gutter with ruling (a vertical frame line is visible
on each block). So the strip looks like the lower or upper part of a bifolium
or of a sheet with two pages, each page a single column. About 10-11 lines
visible per block on face A; similar on face B. No rubrics, no coloured
initials, no running titles visible at overview size. Upper edge of the strip
is ragged and lines may be cut there; holes and staining throughout. Face B
right block is heavily stained (brown spots) and faint.
Tentative: looks like a documentary or notarial/administrative text, or a
draft/register, rather than a book hand; this is impression only.

------------------------------------------------------------------
FACE A (overview image-001), LEFT BLOCK, line beginnings
image-002.jpg (native tile; covers left margin of the strip and the first
c. 4-6 cm of each line of the left block; text starts at x c. 600). Read
with contrast crops crop-01.jpg (lines 1-7) and crop-02.jpg (lines 8-15).
Process note: I opened image-003.jpg once before writing this section (by
mistake, out of order); the readings below are from image-002 and its crops,
which were in view while I wrote them.

Observations: wide blank left margin (c. 4.5 cm), no marginalia visible on
it. 15 lines visible, the last cut at the lower edge. A vertical ruling line
appears to run through the text block (visible in crop-01 at c. x 560 of the
crop) -- possibly a frame line of the left column or a fold. Hand: rapid
current cursive, looped ascenders, long-s and f descending below line, d with
looped back, frequent final -s as a "B"-like sigma form, "9"-shaped con-/-us.
Abbreviations: superscript strokes, p with bar through descender (per/pro),
q with stroke (quod).

image-002 l.1  Ideo ill[?]imus(?) Bar[...]   (first word "Ideo" fairly secure;
               second word could be ill(ustr)i(ssi)mus? -- unsure)
image-002 l.2  nobis(?) dict(us)? / d(omi)ni(?) [...]
image-002 l.3  vero(?) p(er)m(issum)? nobis(?) d[...]
image-002 l.4  c(on)tinuas(?) fi[...] p(re)re[...]   (uncertain throughout)
image-002 l.5  dicte(?) cedule(?) [illegible] e(st)? [...]
image-002 l.6  ut p(re)fat[...]? [illegible] p(ar)t[...]
image-002 l.7  fiat(?) [illegible] [...]
image-002 l.8  Et c(on)sid(er)ant(es)? dict(e)? [...]
image-002 l.9  p(ro)hibent(?) e(t) archi[...]
image-002 l.10 ip(s)os(?) magnos(?) / nostros(?) a[...]
image-002 l.11 cedulas(?) / credens(?) q(uod) p(re)d[...]
image-002 l.12 Et etiam(?) habent(?) est / esse(?)
image-002 l.13 illas(?) cedulas(?) Dut[...]
image-002 l.14 q(u)i(?) ib(?) de [illegible]
image-002 l.15 [cut at lower edge, tops of letters only]

Confidence: low. Most word-shapes are visible but the hand is rapid and I
could not settle many letter forms on line-starts alone.

------------------------------------------------------------------
FACE A, LEFT BLOCK, rest of lines
image-003.jpg (native tile; overlaps image-002 by c. one word: its first
letters "...mus Bar..." on l.1 = end of image-002 l.1). Left c. 920 px carry
the remainder of the left block; a vertical ruling/frame line at c. x 900
closes the block (in crop-04 a stroke on l.11 runs past it). Right part of
the tile (x 920-1399) is the blank central zone (fold/gutter), stained, with
a horizontal crack/crease. Read with crops crop-03.jpg (l.1-7) and
crop-04.jpg (l.8-15). Line numbers match image-002 (same baseline rows).

               (upper edge torn; tops of letters lost)
image-003 l.2  d(omi)ni [illegible] [p...] [illegible]
image-003 l.3  nobis lo(?) p(re)d(ic)t(o)s(?) vel(?) p(re)l(a)t(is)? / pact(is)?

image-003 l.5  [..]de(?) [..] aut(em) / D(omi)ni honorab(i)l(is)? 
               ("honorab-" reasonably clear; final letters uncertain)

               ("atq(ue)" at line end fairly clear)

               (word over/after blot looks like "Septembr-"; uncertain)

               ("sibi" fairly clear)

image-003 l.14 [..]vend[..]enda(?) p(re)tia(?) / parat(?) [..]to(?) p(er)
image-003 l.15 [cut; letter tops only]

Unread / unsettled: nearly every line has unresolved words; this block needs
a second reader with fresh eyes, ideally on a larger-scale or multispectral
image.

------------------------------------------------------------------
FACE A, RIGHT BLOCK, line beginnings
image-004.jpg (native tile). Left c. 600 px = blank central zone (stained,
with a vertical ruling line at c. x 185 and another at c. x 600 that frames
the right block on its left; horizontal crease at c. y 420). The right block
starts at x c. 610. Its text is fainter (grey-brown) than the left block.
About 13-14 lines visible, the top line cut by the torn upper edge and holes
(large hole at top x 650-770; hole at bottom x 1080-1170 damages last 2
lines). Read with crop-05.jpg (top half) and crop-06.jpg (bottom half).
Line numbering here: R1 = first line with readable letter bodies (c. y 210
in image-004); a cut line of traces above it is R0.

image-004 R9  Longas(?) / Concordia(?)  facta(?) [..] ip(s)o(?) / ip(s)a(?)

Confidence: very low on this block; ink is faint and the hand cramped.

------------------------------------------------------------------
FACE A, RIGHT BLOCK, line ends
image-005.jpg (native tile; overlaps image-004 by c. one word per line,
e.g. "alios" on R3 appears at the end of image-004 and the start of
image-005). The right block ends at a vertical frame line at c. x 745; beyond
it a blank margin c. 4.5 cm wide with the modern pencil label
"Stams, STA, Frg. 94 r" (my reading of the label; modern, not part of the
text). A horizontal rule-like line/crack runs across at c. y 935 near the
bottom right of the block. Read with crop-07.jpg. Rows matched to R-numbering

Confidence: very low. Nothing on this face can be called a secure
connected span of ten words; the surest fragments are "Ideo" (A l.1),
"honorab-" (A l.5), "atq(ue)" (A l.6), "sibi" (A l.12), "Septembr-?" (A l.7),
and "alios" (A R3).

==================================================================
FACE B (overview image-006; modern pencil label at bottom centre, read by
me as "Stams, StA, Frg. 94 v"). Same layout as face A: wide left margin,
left text block, blank stained central zone, right text block (much more
